note: The English epigraphs are loose modern paraphrases cited by chapter only (“from John 8”). Each was rendered in the Swahili Union Version (SUV) tradition the shipped sw corpus quotes, not swhonen. Eleven of the twelve are pasted verbatim from a shipped *.sw.json (`mined`); where the SUV verse is fuller or worded differently from the English paraphrase (Psalm 68:5 “mwamuzi wa wajane”, Isaiah 1:17 includes the orphans clause, Romans 5:8 in SUV order, Ezekiel 36:26 “moyo wa nyama”), the SUV wording was kept so the young-reader edition reads as the same Bible as the rest of the sw library.

Self-rendered, needing a native check: Psalm 27:10 (the English is a simplified “Even if my father and my mother leave me, the Lord will take care of me”; no shipped SUV text, rendered plainly), Ramabai’s own “as Abraham, not knowing whither I went” (Hebrews 11:8, re-personed to first person “nisijue niendako”), and her quotation of Job 1:21 in chapter 12 (rendered in the SUV register; the only corpus hit is an expanded LXX-style form quoted by Müller, not used).

Uncited allusions translated as prose, not recorded as references: “Remember the days of old” (chapter 10, cf. Deuteronomy 32:7), “living water” (chapter 7, John 4:10), “while we were still sinners” and “sat in darkness … a great light” echoed in chapter 9’s prose.

Word choices worth a reviewer's eye: “tiger” is “simba milia”; caste is “tabaka”; Mukti is glossed “wokovu, au kuwekwa huru”; Pandita is glossed “mwanamke mwenye elimu” (matching brave-for-god-2.sw); the Portraits of Courage series is named “Picha za Ujasiri” in the attribution. No clock times occur.
